A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research problem and MB-RS-QVI algorithm. Their main texts, equations, and complete proof appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports algorithms, theoretical sample-complexity bounds, and proofs. Neither the main text nor Appendices A–D reports original empirical outcomes.

after.justification: v2 remains theoretical. The additional appendices and Figure 1 provide mathematical definitions, proofs, and a constructed MDP, without experimental or simulation outcomes.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain uniform generative-model sampling, plug-in transition estimation, and risk-sensitive Q-value iteration with a greedy policy. The revised guarantees and expanded mathematical foundations do not change this procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or reports executed training or evaluation tasks. The revised hard-MDP families are theoretical lower-bound constructions.

E2.justification: Both discuss prior algorithms and risk-neutral guarantees, but neither reports an empirical comparison against baseline methods.

E3.justification: Neither PDF reports experimental protocols. Revised sample-size formulas specify theoretical guarantees, without establishing changes to experiments, evaluation metrics, or training budgets actually used.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, empirical sensitivity analyses, robustness experiments, or case-study outcomes. The additional case analyses concern mathematical proofs.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, empirical uncertainty intervals, or significance tests. The added concentration theorem belongs to the theoretical PAC analysis.

E6.justification: Neither PDF contains measured performance values or empirical result entries. Revisions to analytical bounds and proof constants are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: v2 Theorem 1 replaces the SA(S+log(SA/delta)) dependence with SA log(SA/delta) and revises the risk-parameter dependence to permit a finite risk-neutral limit. A new policy bound introduces an additional (1-gamma)^-2 factor; v1's policy bound survives with limited revisions as Theorem 3. Appendices B–E add risk-measure definitions, stationary-optimality and greedy-policy results, and Hoeffding concentration alongside the relocated Weissman lemma. Lemma 3 is strengthened, and revised lower-bound constructions yield (S-2)A and (S-2)(A-1) factors.

C1.justification: The abstract expands claimed tightness from epsilon/delta and tight or nearly tight action dependence to S, A, delta, and epsilon. The introduction and conclusion now emphasize the revised Q-learning bound and two complementary policy bounds. However, Section 1.1's summary of the alternative policy bound omits the factor 2 appearing in Theorem 3's exponential term.

C2.justification: v2 quantifies the new bounds' gaps from risk-neutral guarantees as beta approaches zero. It also explains why the retained policy bound may be preferable for long horizons and small state spaces, while acknowledging its divergence as beta approaches zero. The broader limitations and future directions remain largely unchanged.

D1.justification: The same algorithmic pseudocode and generative-model interface are supplied. v2 adds no implementation resources, hardware or runtime information, experimental hyperparameters, or code/data access instructions.

R1.justification: v2 adds Bäuerle and Jaśkiewicz's 2024 overview and Singh and Yee's 1994 greedy-policy result, and positions its Q-function optimality proof against prior V-function treatments. Most related-work coverage remains. Its discussion of whether prior work covers beta>0 is inconsistent between Section 2.3 and Appendix C.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the prose remain intact. v2 makes localized language edits, corrects erroneous 'non-recursive' wording in the introduction, changes risk notation, and inserts new appendix sections while retaining and relocating existing proofs.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 1 illustrating the theoretical hard-MDP construction and uses denser typesetting. Both retained algorithm displays now appear on page 6. No empirical tables or plots are introduced.

improvement.justification: v2 offers more informative stated bounds, a clearer lower-bound construction, and fuller theoretical foundations. However, the new support has unresolved problems: Theorem 2 invokes Theorem 7's policy defined using the true transition model without connecting it to Algorithm 2's empirical-model policy, and Appendix C's contraction derivation (39–41) contains sign inconsistencies. Together with the incorrect exponential factor in Section 1.1, these issues prevent a confident net assessment of the gains in explanation against the problems in rigor and consistency.
